Article Title: 'Illiterate government': Kejriwal takes aim at Centre over E20 fuel policy, sugar prices
Article Text:
Kejriwal alleged ethanol production from sugarcane had caused a sugar shortage, forcing India to use foreign exchange to import sugar.

Centre rejects mileage link

NEW DELHI: AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday stepped up his criticism of the Centre’s ethanol policy, linking the use of sugarcane for ethanol production to the recent rise in sugar prices and accusing the government of creating a supply problem.In a post on X, Kejriwal said the government had promoted ethanol production from sugarcane to reduce foreign exchange spending on crude oil imports, but was now considering sugar imports because of tighter domestic supplies. “To save the foreign exchange spent on oil imports, they started making ethanol from sugarcane. As a result, there has been a shortage of sugar. Now, they will import sugar using that foreign exchange,” he said.Kejriwal also attacked the government over its handling of the issue, saying, “It's a government entirely run by illiterates. No one knows what will happen if they do something.”His comments come amid a sharp rise in domestic sugar prices and reports that the government is considering measures, including limited imports and tighter stockholding limits, to improve supplies ahead of the festival season.The former Delhi chief minister has also been leading the AAP’s campaign against E20 petrol, alleging that the government is trying to silence criticism of the ethanol-blended fuel policy.In a video posted on X, Kejriwal claimed that social media content critical of E20 was being removed and questioned how public concerns could be suppressed.“Anyone who raises a voice against E20...their page (is) taken down, their video deleted... FIR filed against them... How will you suppress 1.40 crore people?” he said.Kejriwal used a joke about police forces from the US, Russia and India searching for a lion to criticise the government’s handling of the E20 debate. He said people were being pressured to accept that “E20 is right”.AAP has sought greater disclosure of fuel-quality and vehicle-compatibility testing and has argued that consumers should have a choice of conventional petrol at fuel stations.The government has maintained that E20 cannot by itself be blamed for changes in vehicle mileage.The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said on Saturday that E20 had undergone extensive testing and validation, while stressing that real-world fuel economy is affected by factors including driving habits, traffic conditions, vehicle maintenance, tyre pressure and air-conditioner use.“Mileage depends on more than fuel alone. Driving habits, traffic, vehicle maintenance, tyre pressure and AC usage all play a role,” the ministry said.“E20 has undergone extensive testing and validation, while real-world mileage depends on the overall driving and vehicle conditions,” it added.
Article Summary: Kejriwal alleged ethanol production from sugarcane had caused a sugar shortage, forcing india to use foreign exchange to import sugar. He also attacked the government over its handling of the issue, saying, “it's a government entirely run by illiterates”

Article Title: 2.98 lakh URLs sent for takedown; I4C flags scams, CSAM and other unlawful content
Article Text:
2.44 lakh URLs flagged by states for takedown between March and July

Here's what I4C flagged

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nearly 3 lakh URLs were sent to social media platforms for takedown by government departments between March and July 2026, with states accounting for 82% of the requests, the PIB Fact Check unit said. The figures come after articles claiming that Meta had automated content blocking to meet the government's three-hour takedown requirement, with content blocks rising during the Delhiprotests resurfaced.Of the total URLs sent for takedown, 2.44 lakh, or 82%, came from states, while 51,000 were sent by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The I4C requests concerned cyber, infrastructure and stock-investment scams, the government's fact-check body said."During the period from March 2026 to July 2026, around 2.98 lakh URLs were sent for takedown, out of which 2.44 lakhs were sent by states (82 per cent). Of these, 51 thousand URLs were sent by I4C in the context of cyber, infrastructure, and stock-investment scams," the PIB Fact Check account said on X.The PIB Fact Check unit also addressed reports about Meta using automated systems to block content to meet the government's three-hour takedown requirement.It termed the reports misleading and said, "The API integration with Meta took place in 2025 at the request of Meta."The government had amended the IT Intermediaries Rules 2021 in February to speed up the removal of unlawful content. The time given for takedowns was subsequently cut to three hours from 36 hours.According to the fact-check unit, most of the unlawful content flagged by I4C over the past two years was linked to transnational financial frauds, CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material), and offences related to women and children.The unit said the volume of content being posted online also made it necessary for the government to act against unlawful material. With 600 million users in India posting up to 78,703 items every 68 seconds, it said, it was reasonable to expect that, on average, one of those items may not be lawful."The State and its instrumentalities cannot abdicate their responsibilities and allow free rein to lawlessness in cyberspace," PIB Fact Check said.The unit said social media platforms, or IT intermediaries, act on requests sent by competent authorities. It added that only authorised officers notified by the relevant ministry or state government can send requests through Sahyog for the removal of unlawful content."Only authorised officers as notified by the concerned ministry or state government can send intimations for unlawful content takedown through Sahyog. All such intimations are reviewed by the concerned governments periodically," the fact check unit said.
Article Summary: 2.44 lakh urls flagged by states for takedown between march and july 2026. 51,000 were sent by the indian cyber crime coordination centre (i4c) the i4c requests concerned cyber, infrastructure and stock-investment scams.

A viral video showing a group of men dancing to loud music inside a cave in Dehradun has drawn sharp criticism online, with users calling out what they described as a lack of civic sense at a shared tourist spot.The clip, shared on X by an account named @himalayanhindu, was reportedly filmed at Gucchu Paani in Uttarakhand’s capital. It shows the men singing and dancing as they make their way through a section of the cave filled with knee-deep water.One of them can be seen carrying a large speaker, with music playing loudly as the group moves through the cave. The video also shows them blasting a Haryanvi song on the speaker titled "Lofar They Haryana Ke" as they danced. The video has garnered over 404,000 views.The footage prompted several users to criticise the behaviour, with many arguing that visitors should be more mindful of other people and the natural surroundings at tourist destinations.One user wrote, “There is no logic to blame a state, morons are everywhere in our country. Need to deal with them with iron fist ‘on the spot’.”Another user commented, “It is Nothing but mental disease of superiority complex.”“It is infuriating to see these specimens. They cannot even enjoy the place and neither will they allow others to enjoy as well. You need to listen to nature, not blast your nonsense music everywhere,” wrote a user.One user went further, alleging broader misconduct by people behaving in this manner. “They eve tease women and if someone ressists they will attack like a pack of wild dogs. And when they get beaten start crying about how people discriminate them,” the user wrote.Another criticised not only the people seen in the video but also those supporting their behaviour online. “Zero civic sense in people in this video and people defending this in the comments,” the user wrote.No police action has been reported so far, and there has been no official word from local authorities on the video.

Article Title: Trump’s new H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds, greater risks
Article Text:
The H-1B visa route is becoming more selective, compliance-intensive, and less forgiving.

But, Indian professionals who are evaluating career prospects in the US must understand not only the immediate regulatory changes, but also the longer-term implications for career mobility, employer sponsorship and immigration planning. The H-1B visa route is becoming more selective, compliance-intensive, and less forgiving. Here’s what you should know:

USCIS archived the guidance that let terminated workers use B-2 for job search, and immigration attorneys are steering clients away from using B-2 as a bridge as a result. The May 2026 USCIS Adjustment of Status memo now treats in-country green card adjustment as extraordinary discretionary relief. Footnote 20 of the memo says holding H-1B status alone is not sufficient to justify adjustment.

India EB-1 filings jumped from 12,006 in FY2024 to 14,248 in FY2025, and denials on those filings ran at 22% (vs. 9% in FY2024). Indians are pouring into EB-1 as EB-2 stalls, and USCIS is denying more of it.

Has the Donald Trump administration effectively killed the H-1B visa dream? Frequent policy changes, increasing restrictions and selective picking - the H-1B visa path for Indian professionals is becoming tougher to navigate - with unpredictability serving as the biggest obstruction.H-1B visas have long been the main road for Indian professionals who are seeking employment, long-term career opportunities, and eventually even the green card in the US. But over the past two years, several changes in the H-1B visa application and selection criterion have added a huge layer of uncertainty.Which is not to say that Indians still don’t make up the biggest chunk of individuals being granted the H-B visas. This is particularly true for engineering, technology, financial services, healthcare, and research-driven industries.Also Read | Indian IT sector job market is changing: What can get you hired & at a premium Higher H-1B application fee (under litigation as of now), a new selection process, new rules for the 60-day grace period - the process has seen several changes recently.Xiao Wang, CEO of Boundless Immigration points out the three things that have changed in the last year, and how they are compounding the uncertainty:First, the $100,000 fee. Boundless’ CEO is of the view that the fee has dissuaded external applications from India in the first cap season under it, and that India-based IT consulting firms have absorbed the biggest hit, since their model depends on sending people to the US from India.“The National Foundation for American Policy documented the shift on the employer side: the top four H-1B employers in FY2025 are Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Google, not the Indian IT firms that historically held those slots,” Xiao Wang tells TOI.The fee has recently been struck down by a US court, but is likely to be appealed by the Trump administration.Second, the wage-weighted lottery. USCIS ran the March 2026 cap season under new rules that favor higher-paid workers. “In our Boundless client data, Level III (senior) candidates were selected at 68%, and Level I (entry level) candidates at 40%. For Indian professionals coming out of US master's programs into their first job, that gap matters,” he says.Third, the sharp drop in EB-1A approvals. The USCIS I-140 report for Q2 FY2026 (Jan-Mar 2026) puts the EB-1A approval rate at 41.7%, down from 66.9% for FY2025 as a whole.In the same USCIS I-140 country data, Indian nationals filed 1,761 of the 6,647 EB-1A receipts worldwide in Q2 FY2026, 26.5% of the total.“Our read is that the drop in approvals lands disproportionately on Indian applicants because they are the single largest filer population in the category,” he says.According to K Edward Raleigh, Partner at Fragomen, a global immigration law firm, the new selection system gives greater weight to higher-paid and higher-skilled positions rather than relying on a purely random selection process.“That potentially creates advantages for some highly skilled professionals while making the process more challenging for others,” he tells TOI.Once you have received an H-1B visa, the road is somewhat smoother. Experts say renewing the H-1B is still a routine process.According to Boundless, the NFAP November 2025 report puts the continuing employment denial rate at 1.9% for FY2025, which is essentially unchanged from 1.8% in FY2024.But, there are risks associated with layoffs, which then initiates the 60-day grace period for visa holders to find an alternative job.“An H-1B worker who does not line up a new sponsoring employer or change status within 60 days falls out of status,” notes Xiao Wang, adding that two protections that used to make that window survivable are now weaker.There is also an added factor: The cost of keeping an existing H-1B worker could become more expensive. The Trump administration is considering extending the additional $4,000 H-1B fee and $4,500 L-1 fee to extensions for certain large employers.The proposal would particularly affect companies heavily dependent on foreign workers. About 71% of H-1B approvals in FY2025 were for continuing employment, and Indians accounted for nearly 78% of H-1B extensions.Meanwhile, the Department of Homeland Security is advancing a proposal to eliminate the 60-day grace period that currently allows H-1B workers who lose their jobs to find another sponsor, change status or prepare to leave.The proposal is not yet law, but if implemented, losing a job would create a much tighter immigration deadline and increase workers' dependence on their sponsoring employer.Why the 60-day grace period changes are worrying is because of the labour market.“It’s a labor market affected by layoffs and AI-driven restructuring. An H-1B employee faces both the ordinary consequences of losing a job and an immigration consequence,” says K Edward Raleigh of Fragomen.“How difficult it is to find another sponsor within the available period depends heavily on the individual’s skills, seniority, industry and the willingness of prospective employers to undertake sponsorship,” he tells TOI, adding that employers continue to compete for exceptional talent, particularly in areas such as AI and machine learning.Also Read | Harsh reality for H-1B visa returnees: Changed Indian IT hiring landscape, lower salaries and fewer jobs But even as Boundless’ Xiao Wang acknowledges the vulnerability, he tells TOI that the labour market picture is more mixed than the layoff headlines.“The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) unemployment rate for computer and mathematical occupations was 3.0% in August 2025, down from 3.4% a year earlier. USCIS approved 68,167 H-1B transfers in FY2025, and roughly 37% of H-1B workers who started at a new employer that year moved through the transfer route rather than through a new cap petition,” he explains.“We're hearing more mid-career Indian H-1B workers ask about self-petition options (O-1, EB-2 NIW, EB-1A) as insurance policies before they need them,” he says.According to Boundless’ CEO, for an Indian applicant, the deeper issue is the green card queue.“USCIS I-140 data puts India's EB-2 pending inventory at 351,142 petitions and EB-3 pending at 105,588. Cato Institute analysis by David Bier projects the EB-2 India wait for a new filing today at multiple decades under current visa issuance rates. Indian H-1B holders are therefore usually stuck on H-1B for many years, and losing a job during that window is a sharper cliff than for most other nationalities,” he cautions.Even as uncertainties mount, applications are still outpacing the allowed slots. Registrations still exceed slots by roughly five to one, says Xiao Wang. In the last posted H-1B registration cycle, USCIS had about 442,000 unique beneficiaries chasing 85,000 slots.Demand for the visa is not the constraint. What's changing is where the next generation of Indian technologists choose to build a career.Britta Glennon's Wharton research, cited in the NFAP report, finds that when US firms lose H-1B access they set up foreign affiliates and hire there at close to a one-for-one rate.“So global demand for the workers is not the constraint. Our read is that what has shifted is where the marginal Indian technologist bets, with Canada, the UK, Australia, and Germany picking up more of the flow,” Xiao Wang tells TOI.On the employer side, NFAP reports that the top seven India-based IT companies received 4,573 initial H-1B approvals in FY2025, a 37% drop from FY2024 and a 70% drop from FY2015. US tech companies now hold the top four employer slots for new H-1B approvals.So what do all these developments mean for Indian professionals? Experts are unanimous that caution is warranted and the environment continues to be volatile.Boundless Immigration CEO says that for Indian applicants, the H-1B is still a viable entry point, but applicants need to enter with realistic expectations.“H-1B is still a viable pathway if the applicant accepts that it may mean spending many years in temporary status rather than moving quickly to permanent residence,” Wang tells TOI. He shares some interesting data insights: The India numbers, from the USCIS I-140 report through Q2 FY2026For an early-career Indian engineer today, Canada may offer permanent residence far sooner than the US, he adds.Experts note that specialised skills continue to be in demand, and that would be the way forward as well.Akhil Chandna, Partner and Global People Solutions Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat believes that success in getting H-1B visas and retaining jobs in the US is likely to depend on a combination of specialised skills, career progression, employer sponsorship strategies and proactive immigration planning.“Professionals who remain aligned with high-demand sectors and invest in continuous upskilling are likely to be better positioned for long-term success,” he tells TOI.“Despite increased scrutiny, layoffs, and immigration uncertainty, the H-1B remains one of the most established routes for Indian professionals seeking a long-term career in the US. The US has however become less attractive for early-career professionals. Alternative countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom and Australia remain attractive,” he adds.“Professionals should focus on building differentiated skills, maintaining strong documentation of specialized expertise and evaluating immigration options with broader career goals. Early planning can help manage uncertainty and improve resilience across career transitions,” he recommends.K Edward Raleigh at Fragomen sums it up: The H-1B environment has undoubtedly become more complex and less forgiving in recent years. We are seeing a greater emphasis on immigration compliance and vetting, along with structural changes to the H-1B program.According to Raleigh, for Indian professionals looking at the US over the longer term, the distinction between temporary H-1B status and permanent residence is important.The H-1B can provide a durable means of working in the US, including in certain circumstances through extensions beyond the normal six-year limit while a Green Card case is pending. At the same time, India-born professionals face significant employment-based Green Card backlogs, which can create considerable uncertainty around the timing of permanent residence.“Those realities make long-term immigration planning increasingly important for both employees and employers,” he says.
Article Summary: The h-1b visa route is becoming more selective, compliance-intensive, and less forgiving. Indian professionals who are evaluating career prospects in the us must understand the longer-term implications for career mobility and employer sponsorship.

Article Title: NHL Trade Rumors: Cutter Gauthier camp rejects Anaheim Ducks contract offer as Pavel Zacha's Boston Bruins future remains uncertain
Article Text:
Cutter Gauthier (Credit: Getty Images)

Why has Cutter Gauthier turned down the Anaheim Ducks' contract offer?

What does Pavel Zacha's contract situation mean for the Boston Bruins?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Will Pavel Zacha stay with the Boston Bruins or become a trade candidate?

The Anaheim Ducks and Boston Bruins are facing two contract situations that could shape their plans for the upcoming NHL season. Cutter Gauthier is coming off a breakout year in Anaheim, while Pavel Zacha is entering the final season of his current deal in Boston.Both players have reasons to attract attention around the league. Gauthier has put himself in a strong position after his latest season, while Zacha’s future could become a bigger talking point as the Bruins weigh their options before the trade deadline.Gauthier is coming off his entry-level contract after scoring 41 goals and 69 points last season. The 21-year-old winger does not have arbitration rights and also cannot sign an offer sheet because he has not played enough NHL games to qualify. That normally would give Anaheim more control in contract talks. However, Gauthier’s production gives him a strong reason to ask for a much bigger deal.On Sunday, NHL Network Radio’s Paul Shaheen said reliable sources told him that Gauthier’s camp rejected a four-year contract worth an average annual value of $13 million. Shaheen also said the Ducks may need to get creative with their salary cap situation if and when Gauthier signs.The problem comes from Leo Carlsson’s new contract. Anaheim matched the Philadelphia Flyers’ five-year, $90 million offer sheet for Carlsson last month, giving him an $18 million annual average value. According to PuckPedia, the Ducks have just over $9 million in cap space, making it difficult to sign a new deal for Gauthier without moving salary.Sportsnet’s Emily Sadler also pointed to the cap issue. Anaheim will get some relief next summer when Chris Kreider and Alex Killorn become unrestricted free agents, but the Ducks still have to find a way to fit Gauthier into their current plans.The situation around Pavel Zacha is different, but his future in Boston is also worth watching. The 29-year-old center is entering the final season of his four-year contract, which carries a $4.75 million AAV. Unless he signs an extension, he will become an unrestricted free agent next July.Boston Herald’s Steve Conroy believes Zacha has been a reliable player for Boston and could still have a place on the team. However, his trade value may be higher than ever, which could give the Bruins another option. There is another factor for Boston to consider. Re-signing Zacha could make it harder for young centers such as Fraser Minten, James Hagens or Dean Letourneau to move into bigger roles.The Bruins are believed to want Zacha back, but he was also part of trade speculation earlier this offseason. Conroy noted that Boston is unlikely to move him without getting a deal done before the season begins. His situation could become more interesting around the March 1 trade deadline if the Bruins are out of playoff contention.For now, Anaheim needs to solve its cap situation before getting Gauthier signed, while Boston must decide whether Zacha is part of its long-term plans or could become a valuable trade piece.
Article Summary: Cutter gauthier is coming off a breakout year in anaheim. Pavel zacha is entering the final season of his current deal in boston. The bruins are believed to want zacha back, but he was also part of trade speculation earlier this offseason.

Article Title: Valkyrae’s AI controversy grows as streamer reveals the artist behind her disputed YouTube thumbnail
Article Text:
Valkyrae addresses AI allegations over YouTube thumbnail

Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko

Rachell “Valkyrae” Hofstetter has addressed a growing debate over the artwork used for her YouTube livestreams after viewers accused her latest thumbnail of being AI-generated. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, Anko, while admitting she understands why some people reached that conclusion. Her comments also highlight a wider concern for digital artists as AI-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.The controversy began after Anko, Valkyrae’s thumbnail artist, shared the creative process behind artwork for her Uncharted playthrough. The thumbnail initially received attention from viewers, but some quickly questioned whether artificial intelligence had been used to create it.That reaction eventually reached Valkyrae, who explained that Anko creates all of her YouTube livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his process online. She also pointed out the irony of the situation, saying that even those behind-the-scenes videos have not stopped people from making AI accusations.Valkyrae said:"Okay. We have to talk about this thumbnail debacle. I don't know what to do about this thumbnail debacle.So, as most of you know, every single one of my YouTube livestream thumbnails is made by the same artist. His name is Anko, and he makes all of them. He even posts on Twitter the art process of making them, but it still never beats the AI allegations. And the most recent thumbnail, he makes new thumbnails when I start a new game series, so, obviously, there is a new thumbnail for the Uncharted era. And people were saying, 'Oh, it's AI slop,' in the pre-chat."The streamer then offered a more nuanced response. Rather than dismissing viewers who suspected AI, she said she understood where their reaction came from. At the same time, she wanted to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI.Valkyrae added:"'Just ignore them.' Well, no. Okay? I don't blame people for thinking it's AI because AI is using people's art, like Anko's, to take over. But I would like to clear it up because there were a few people that were saying, 'Oh! When I saw the thumb, I also thought it was AI.' So now I am wondering how many people are out there that would watch the stream, but didn't because of the AI-looking thumbnail! But it's not AI."The discussion also became personal for Valkyrae because she said she felt bad for Anko. The thumbnail was later updated, with the artist adding his signature, giving viewers another indication of who created the work.Valkyrae explained that the situation made her think about the broader impact AI tools could have on working artists. For creators who depend on commissioned digital artwork, being mistaken for AI-generated work can create a difficult problem. The visual style that once helped an artist stand out can now cause audiences to question whether a human created it at all.She said:"I don't know, dude. I don't know what to do about it. I feel bad for him, though, because... and then, it, like, reminded me. I was like, 'Man, I just shouldn't do art thumbnails.' But then, the whole AI thing is doing what it does - making artists lose their jobs! Isn't that crazy?!"The controversy has now become more than a discussion about one YouTube thumbnail. Valkyrae’s response reflects a growing tension between AI-generated imagery and human-made digital art, particularly on social media where polished artwork can be judged within seconds.For Valkyrae, however, the message is straightforward: the Uncharted thumbnail was made by Anko, not AI. The debate instead shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.
Article Summary: Valkyrae addresses ai allegations over youtube thumbnail. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, anko. Her comments highlight a wider concern for digital artists as ai-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: Microsoft AI's chief marketing officer, Andra Mallard, is leaving the company, just 6 months after she joined; read email to employees
Article Text:

A shift in Microsoft's AI marketing strategy

Part of a broader reshuffle at Microsoft AI

Mallard's background

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe Microsoft should replace Mallard in the CMO role? Yes, they need strong leadership for marketing. No, consolidating responsibilities is a better approach. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

What she worked on during her short tenure

Microsoft has confirmed that Andra Mallard, chief marketing officer of its AI unit, is leaving the company just six months after joining from Pinterest. According to a memo, viewed by Business Insider, Microsoft executive Yusuf Mehdi told employees that Mallard plans to relocate her family to Europe in August to be closer to her ailing father, leading her to step back from her role. Microsoft confirmed Mallard's departure plans, noting she will remain with the company until early next year in an advisory capacity. In the memo, Mehdi expressed appreciation for the energy and consumer-focused approach Mallard brought to accelerating Microsoft's Copilot marketing efforts, crediting her with helping push a more unified strategy, including the push toward a single app experience.“I’m grateful for the incredible energy and consumer‑centric ethos she’s brought to turbo‑charging our Copilot marketing efforts; Andrea has played a key role in advocating for a more unified approach, including the single app experience.”According to two people familiar with the matter, Mallard's exit also reflects a broader strategic shift underway at Microsoft AI as the company reconsiders its approach to consumer marketing. Microsoft is in the process of merging its separate consumer and business Copilot apps into a single unified application. Copilot, the company's flagship generative AI product, has generally trailed behind rival AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude in consumer adoption.Going forward, Copilot marketing responsibilities are being consolidated under Microsoft executive Jared Spataro, and the company does not plan to directly replace Mallard's CMO role.Mallard's departure comes amid a period of broader change within Microsoft AI, the unit where she had been hired as CMO. In March, Microsoft moved Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman into a new role focused on a superintelligence-focused team, while also consolidating its various commercial and consumer Copilot teams under new leadership.Mallard brought significant consumer marketing experience to the role. She spent more than seven years as Pinterest's chief marketing officer before joining Microsoft, and prior to that, led marketing at Gap's athleisure brand Athleta and served as CMO at virtual care company Omada Health.During her brief time at Microsoft, marketing initiatives included a Super Bowl advertisement showing NFL teams using Copilot in Excel to analyze athlete performance data and build scouting profiles of top prospects. Microsoft also worked with influencers such as Alix Earle, who has posted content featuring Copilot on her social media channels. Both of these projects, however, had begun before Mallard joined the company.
Article Summary: Andra mallard, microsoft's chief marketing officer of its ai unit, is leaving the company. Mallard plans to relocate her family to europe in august to be closer to her ailing father, leading her to step back from her role. Her departure comes amid a period of broader change within microsoft ai, the unit where she had been hired.

Article Title: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar to employees: Stop worrying about Anthropic; there is a chance they pull off the cover from ...
Article Text:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar characterised the IPO not as an end point but as another step

Addressing the Anthropic question directly

OpenAI’s financial performance

Turnover in the executive ranks

OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar has told the employees during a recent all-hands meeting that the ChatGPT-maker “will be a public company in 2027,” though the debut could come sooner if business momentum continues, as reported by CNBC. “The IPO is not a finish line, it is a milestone, another fundraise,” she said, noting that OpenAI raised $122 billion in March, giving it flexibility. Friar addressed concerns about competitor Anthropic, which has also confidentially filed for an IPO. She told employees not to worry if Anthropic goes public first. “There is a chance they pull the cover off that confidential file in the coming weeks and become public in September. That’s OK, we are running our own race,” she said, according to sources.Friar characterized the IPO not as an end point but as another step in the company's fundraising journey, telling employees, according to the sources, that the IPO is not a finish line, it is a milestone. She pointed to the $122 billion OpenAI raised in March as a source of continued flexibility for the company going forward.OpenAI confidentially filed its IPO prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June but has not publicly disclosed a specific debut date.Its chief rival, Anthropic, has also confidentially filed its own prospectus with regulators and has reportedly been holding early meetings to gauge interest from potential investors.Friar used part of the meeting to get ahead of employee concerns that Anthropic might beat OpenAI to the public markets. She told staff that both companies are currently under confidential filing, and that there's a real chance Anthropic could make its filing public in the coming weeks and complete its debut as early as September. According to the sources, Friar told employees that would be fine, since OpenAI is focused on running its own race rather than measuring itself against Anthropic's timeline.OpenAI is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation ahead of a public listing, with investors pushing for more visibility into the company's financials. During the all-hands meeting, Friar shared slides showing that OpenAI's revenue run rate is up 35% quarter to date, its enterprise revenue run rate is up 50% quarter to date, and that its AI coding and work product tools have reached 20 million weekly active users.Separately, OpenAI told investors it generated $6.7 billion in revenue in the second quarter, up 18% from the first quarter, according to a Wall Street Journal report published later Wednesday. The company's annualized revenue run rate has recently topped $40 billion.Anthropic, meanwhile, told its own investors over the weekend that its annualized revenue run rate reached $65 billion by the end of July, a sevenfold increase from a year earlier, alongside a preliminary second-quarter revenue figure of $11.5 billion.Friar's remarks come after a stretch of executive departures at OpenAI that have reportedly left some of the company's financial backers uneasy about potential instability at the top. Revenue chief Denise Dresser left her role last week after just eight months at the company, two days after longtime executive Brad Lightcap announced he was ending an eight-year run at OpenAI to pursue a new venture. In July, product and business chief Fidji Simo stepped down from her role to focus on recovering from a chronic illness.With that turnover in the background, remaining leaders, including Friar, CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman, now face the task of projecting stability to investors already navigating concerns about rising competition, the growing adoption of cheaper open-weight AI models, and the volatile stock performance of SpaceX in its first two months as a public company.
Article Summary: Openai cfo sarah friar addressed concerns about competitor anthropic, which has also confidentially filed for an ipo. She told employees not to worry if anthropic goes public first. “there is a chance they pull the cover off that confidential file in the coming weeks and become public in september,” she said.

The biggest AI companies have spent the past few years fighting for office workers, coders and consumers. Their next battleground may be far more consequential: the classroom. Google this week rolled out a clutch of new learning features across Search and Gemini, including customised quizzes, interactive visualisations, study notebooks and 3D simulations. Students can upload class notes, PDFs and slides and have AI turn them into study material. Gemini is also getting a dedicated Student Hub. Google has also announced 'Back to College' offer, that gives one year of Google AI Plus at no cost to eligible college students across India. The benefits include free access to Gemini Omni, 2x higher usage limits in Gemini, 400GB of storage, and more. Students can also avail a bundle of Google AI Pro and YouTube Premium at up to 70% discount.OpenAI, meanwhile, has launched ChatGPT for Teens, aimed at users aged 13-17. Along with tighter safety controls, the product includes Study Mode, quizzes and prompts designed to stop students from simply asking the chatbot to complete their homework. Last year, the company launched ChatGPT Go at Rs 300 per month. The plan offers unlimited text chats with GPT-5.6 Luna and few other benefits.Coming back to Google and OpenAI tapping students, the timing can be seen as hardly accidental.Students are already using AI. The companies are now trying to make sure they use their AI. Research by Pew earlier this year found that 54% of US teenagers had used chatbots for schoolwork and 57% had used them to search for information. A Common Sense Media study found that 67% of children aged 9-17 had used AI chatbots, with ChatGPT the most frequently mentioned service.There is a familiar Silicon Valley logic at work here: Habits formed early can be extremely difficult to break. Google became synonymous with internet search partly because an entire generation grew up “Googling” things. Microsoft spent decades pushing Office into schools and universities, knowing that students familiar with Word, Excel and PowerPoint would eventually carry those habits into workplaces.AI companies now have a similar opportunity. A student who uses Gemini to revise for an exam today could use it to write reports, analyse spreadsheets or prepare presentations when entering the workforce. A teenager accustomed to asking ChatGPT for explanations may eventually turn to it for coding, research, travel, financial information or work.That makes education strategically valuable even if teenagers themselves are not particularly lucrative customers. Google has already been courting college students with free access to paid Gemini features, while both Google and OpenAI are building products for schools and teachers alongside their student offerings.The prize, therefore, isn't merely subscription revenue from students. It is becoming the default AI interface for a generation. And there is another advantage. Education gives generative AI companies something they badly need: a use case that can be explained easily.“Ask AI anything” can sound vague. “Use AI to prepare for tomorrow's chemistry exam” does not. Quizzes, flashcards, personalised explanations and step-by-step tutoring are tangible applications that showcase exactly why somebody might want an AI assistant in the first place.There is an obvious problem with this strategy: AI can make completing schoolwork easier without necessarily making students better at learning. That distinction explains why both Google and OpenAI increasingly describe their products as tutors rather than answer machines.OpenAI's Study Mode is explicitly designed to take students through problems using questions and step-by-step guidance instead of immediately producing an answer. Its teen product can also detect when a user appears to be trying to shortcut homework and encourage them to use Study Mode instead.Google is following much the same route, surrounding Gemini with quizzes, interactive exercises and learning tools rather than simply improving its ability to spit out answers. That shift matters because schools are still grappling with plagiarism and AI-assisted cheating. Around six in ten US teens surveyed by Pew said students at their schools use AI chatbots to cheat at least sometimes.AI assistants are unusually intimate technology. Unlike a search engine, a chatbot holds conversations, remembers context and can appear remarkably human. Pew found that 12% of teens had already used chatbots for emotional support or advice.OpenAI's new teen experience consequently places stronger restrictions around self-harm, sexual content and other sensitive subjects, while adding parental controls and age estimation. The launch comes amid intense scrutiny of chatbot safety and litigation involving interactions between AI systems and minors.For AI companies, that creates an unusual trade-off. Teenagers may be among their most valuable long-term users, but they are also among the users requiring the strongest protections.Will the strategy pay off? Almost certainly in terms of adoption. AI has already entered classrooms regardless of whether schools formally embrace it. Turning that behaviour into structured learning products is more sensible than pretending students will stop using chatbots.The bigger uncertainty is whether today's winners will retain those users. Switching between AI assistants is far easier than moving between operating systems or social networks. There is little stopping a student from using Gemini for research, ChatGPT for explanations and another model for coding.So the race isn't merely to get students using AI first. It is to become the AI they instinctively open first.
Article Summary: Google rolls out gemini and chatgpt for students. Students can upload class notes, pdfs and slides and have ai turn them into study material. Google has also announced 'back to college' offer, that gives one year of google ai plus at no cost to eligible college students across india.

Article Title: Steve Jobs’ 8th-grade science project becomes an auction sensation as bids reached $8,475
Article Text:
Image: Left/RR Auction/Right/AI Genera​ted

From Steve Jobs’ school science fair project to a sought-after piece of Apple history

The project stayed with the Jobs family for decades

Bidding has pushed the project into five figures of interest

Other Apple memorabilia is also drawing big bids

A glimpse of the inventor before Apple

Long before Steve Jobs helped build Apple into one of the world’s most influential technology companies, he was already experimenting with electronics. A science project Jobs created while he was in eighth grade has now resurfaced decades later, offering collectors a rare glimpse into his early interest in technology. The project, titled “What is the Silicon-Controlled Rectifier?”, is part of an auction of Steve Jobs and Apple memorabilia marking Apple’s 50th anniversary. The collection includes vintage computers, signed documents, advertising material and other objects connected to Jobs and Apple’s early history.The project dates to February 29, 1968, when Jobs was an eighth-grade student. Rather than producing a conventional school display, he chose to explore the silicon-controlled rectifier, or SCR, a semiconductor device used to control electrical power. The surviving project consists of a large tri-fold display explaining the technology, along with demonstration circuits designed to show how the component worked. It also includes a written report and circuit diagrams created by Jobs. The project offers an unusually personal connection to Jobs because it predates the formation of Apple by several years. At the time, he was still a school student experimenting with electronics, long before he became associated with the development of personal computing.One small detail makes the project even more distinctive. Jobs left instructions for the science fair judges explaining how to use the circuits and reminding them to unplug the equipment afterwards. The warning suggests that the young Jobs was already paying close attention to how his technical work should be handled.Unlike many school projects that disappear after a science fair ends, this one remained within Jobs’ family for decades. According to a report by AppleInsider, the project comes from the personal collection of Jobs’ stepbrother, John Chovanec. It had remained at the Jobs family home in Los Altos before eventually becoming part of Chovanec’s collection. That provenance adds another layer of significance for collectors. The object is not simply an old electronics project associated with a famous person; it is a physical artefact from Jobs’ childhood that survived for more than half a century. Its survival also provides a rare look at Jobs before Apple existed. Much of the memorabilia associated with him comes from his professional career, particularly Apple’s early years. This project instead captures a much earlier stage of his life, when his interest in electronics was still developing.The science project is being sold as part of RR Auction’s “Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction Part Two”. The auction contains more than 200 lots connected to Jobs, Apple and the history of personal computing. By August 19, bidding on the science project had reached $8,475, with the auction scheduled to close on August 20 at 6 p.m. Eastern Time. The auction house expects the project could ultimately sell for more than $20,000. The rising price reflects the unusual combination of technological history, personal provenance and Jobs’ connection to the object. A school science project might normally have little monetary value, but this one has become a piece of the story behind one of the world's most recognisable technology companies.The science project is only one part of the auction. Other lots offer collectors objects from different stages of Apple’s development, including vintage computers, components, advertising material and documents connected to Jobs. Among the more valuable items is an Apple-1 computer housed inside a Smith-Corona typewriter case. A Steve Jobs-signed Apple business card is also included, alongside other early Apple material. The auction follows an earlier sale that demonstrated just how much collectors are willing to pay for important pieces of Apple history. In the first part of the anniversary auction, the first cheque issued by Apple sold for $2.4 million, while an Apple-1 prototype board reached $2.75 million. Against those multimillion-dollar sales, Jobs’ eighth-grade project is a much smaller artefact. Yet its appeal comes from something those later objects cannot provide, it shows the future Apple co-founder before Apple existed.The value of Jobs’ science project ultimately goes beyond the electronics mounted on its wooden display. It captures an early moment in the life of someone who would later have an enormous influence on personal technology. The project does not show the finished products, dramatic launches or corporate milestones that later defined Jobs’ career. Instead, it shows a schoolboy investigating how a semiconductor worked and building a practical demonstration around it. That makes the object particularly compelling as Apple reaches its 50th anniversary. The company’s history is usually told through the Apple-1, Macintosh, iPod, iPhone and other landmark products. This small eighth-grade project offers a much earlier chapter, a physical reminder that the story of Jobs’ technological curiosity began long before the Apple logo became globally recognised. What began as an eighth-grade science experiment has now become a rare piece of technology history, with collectors bidding for a glimpse of Steve Jobs before he became Steve Jobs.
